name: Giza Plateau
desc: Three royal pyramid complexes, the Sphinx, workers’ settlements and cemeteries. Explore a millennium-spanning historical model with archival evidence and changing interpretations.
fact: Khufu's pyramid is the only surviving Ancient Wonder of the World.

name: Hawara Labyrinth
focus: Ancient testimony, lost architecture, field research
desc: Amenemhat III’s pyramid and vast cult precinct; later descriptions of an extraordinary labyrinth are compelling, but no archaeologically verified complete floorplan survives.
fact: Herodotus reported 3,000 rooms; that figure is an ancient account, not a surveyed count.

name: Göbekli Tepe
desc: Monumental circular enclosures and carved T-shaped stone pillars reveal impressive communal building before pottery and urban civilizations.
fact: The monumental structures belong to the early Neolithic, long before the pyramids.

name: Stonehenge
desc: A prehistoric monument embedded in a wider landscape of burial mounds, processional routes and changing ceremonies.
fact: Its stone circles developed in multiple phases over many centuries.

name: Petra
date: flourished c. 1st c. BCE–2nd c. CE
desc: Nabataean caravan-city cut into sandstone cliffs; monumental facades and sophisticated water engineering connected trade routes across Arabia and the Mediterranean.
fact: Its landscape combines rock-cut architecture with a sophisticated water system.

name: Machu Picchu
desc: A royal Inca estate set high above the Urubamba River, built with terraces, water channels and precisely worked stone architecture.
fact: Its engineered terraces helped manage steep Andean terrain.

name: Angkor
desc: A vast ceremonial and urban landscape of Khmer temples, canals, reservoirs and royal capitals, including Angkor Wat.
fact: The monumental landscape extends far beyond a single temple.

name: Chichén Itzá
desc: A major Maya urban and ceremonial center whose surviving architecture includes El Castillo, a ballcourt and observatory-related structures.
fact: The site reflects regional political and cultural changes over centuries.

name: Teotihuacan
desc: One of ancient Mesoamerica’s largest cities, organized around the Avenue of the Dead and its Sun and Moon pyramids.
fact: Its city-scale layout reveals remarkable planning and social organization.

name: Borobudur
desc: A monumental Buddhist sanctuary with relief galleries and stupas that unfold as a pilgrimage through successive symbolic levels.
fact: Its sculpture program and architecture work together as a ceremonial journey.

name: Rapa Nui
desc: An island cultural landscape known for its monumental moai, ceremonial platforms and remarkable Polynesian history.
fact: Moai were made in a wider social and ritual landscape, not as isolated sculptures.

name: Nan Madol
desc: Artificial islets and monumental basalt walls create a distinctive ceremonial center built among the tidal waters of Pohnpei.
fact: Its monumental enclosures stand on a network of constructed islets.

name: Tikal
desc: Towering temple pyramids rise above a Maya urban landscape of palaces, roads, reservoirs and carved historical monuments.
fact: Its inscriptions and monuments help reconstruct royal histories.

name: Great Zimbabwe
desc: Sophisticated dry-stone walling and enclosures mark a major southern African center embedded in far-reaching trade networks.
fact: Its monumental walls were built without mortar.

name: Pompeii
desc: An unusually preserved Roman town whose streets, workshops, homes and wall paintings reveal daily urban life before Vesuvius erupted in 79 CE.
fact: The eruption preserved detailed traces of ordinary Roman life.

name: Colosseum & Rome
desc: The Flavian Amphitheatre sits within the extraordinarily layered urban history of Rome, from ancient imperial monuments to later adaptation.
fact: The Colosseum is part of a much larger evolving historic city.

name: Great Wall
date: multiple phases; surviving sector largely Ming
desc: A monumental network of border defenses built and rebuilt by different Chinese states and dynasties over many centuries.
fact: It is not one wall constructed in a single campaign or dynasty.

name: Taj Mahal
desc: A Mughal funerary monument conceived as an integrated garden, riverfront and marble architectural ensemble.
fact: Its decorative stone inlay is part of a unified architectural composition.

name: Abu Simbel
desc: Two rock-cut temples of Ramesses II and Nefertari, famously relocated in the twentieth century to protect them from the rising reservoir.
fact: The modern relocation was itself an enormous international conservation undertaking.

name: Sigiriya
desc: An immense rock citadel whose palace landscape contains gardens, hydraulic features and extraordinary painted surfaces.
fact: Its designed gardens combine landscape, water and architecture.

name: Mohenjo-daro
desc: A major Indus urban settlement with planned streets, sophisticated drainage and distinct public and domestic architecture.
fact: Its planned drainage systems testify to complex ancient urban infrastructure.

name: Lalibela
desc: An interconnected complex of rock-hewn churches, passageways and sacred landscapes that continues as a living place of worship.
fact: The churches were carved downward from living rock.

name: Persepolis
desc: Achaemenid ceremonial terraces and monumental palaces whose reliefs illuminate the imperial court and its global connections.
fact: Stone reliefs show delegations and courtly imagery rather than a complete picture of imperial life.

name: Sacsayhuamán & Cusco
desc: Monumental fitted-stone walls above Cusco, part of the Inca capital and a broader cultural landscape transformed during and after Spanish conquest.
fact: The great stone walls show exceptional fitted masonry without modern machine cutting.
